title: Payer Program Schedule Note — Approval Kinds and Block Counting for Model Change Grants, Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program
content:
Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program — payer approval kinds. On an authorization grant Larkfield records for a new written order of the CGM supply allowance (A4239) that changes the CGM model under the payer authorization already in force, the 30-day blocks of the grant's span, which runs from the order date through the grant's valid-through date, are counted according to the kind of approval that payer authorization is.

### Schedule clause

The approval-period adjustment replaces the standard count of whole blocks of the span by the kind of payer approval:
- **per-period approval:** when the payer authorization is a per-period approval, every 30-day block begun from the order date through the grant's valid-through date counts, a part block counted whole (the days of the span divided by 30, rounded up);
- **approval for fewer units:** when it approved fewer units than the whole blocks of its span times the tier's allowance, the whole blocks count (the days of the grant's span divided by 30, remainder dropped), never more than its units left;
- **approval for more units:** otherwise, when it approved more units than the whole blocks of its span times the tier's allowance, the standard count applies (the days of the grant's span divided by 30, remainder dropped).

The count this schedule gives takes the place of the standard count of whole blocks of the grant's span.

In the two comparisons "its span" is the payer authorization's own span, from its valid-from date through its valid-through date, and "the tier's allowance" is the tier's sensor allowance units per 30 days of supply.

The days of the grant's span are counted from the order date through the grant's valid-through date, both days included.

### Defined terms

- **The payer authorization** is the authorization grant the program's latest refill shipment of the CGM supply allowance drew on.
- **Its whole blocks** are the calendar days from its valid-from date through its valid-through date, both dates counted, divided by 30 with any remainder dropped.
- **Per-period approval:** its units authorized equal its whole blocks multiplied by the tier's sensor allowance units per 30 days of supply. **Fewer units:** its units authorized are below that product. **More units:** they are above it. The allowance is 1 on every tier:

| Tier | Sensor allowance units per 30 days |
|---|---|
| CGM Self-Pay Program | 1 |
| CGM Commercial HMO Program | 1 |
| CGM Commercial PPO Program | 1 |
| CGM Medicare Advantage Program | 1 |
| CGM Original Medicare Program | 1 |
| CGM Medicaid Program | 1 |

- **Units left** are the units it authorized less the billing units of the refill shipments of the CGM supply allowance drawn on it, never fewer than none.

### Schedule illustrations (hypothetical figures)

Suppose a payer authorization valid 1 January through 30 June of a non-leap year: 181 days, 6 whole blocks. Suppose the new order is dated 1 March and the grant is valid through 30 June: a span of 122 days.

| Units the payer authorization approved | Refill units drawn on it | Kind | Blocks counted for the grant |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6 | any | per-period approval (6 equals 6 multiplied by 1) | 122 days divided by 30, rounded up: 5 |
| 4 | 2 (units left 2) | fewer units | 4 whole blocks, held to the 2 units left: 2 |
| 4 | 0 (units left 4) | fewer units | 4 whole blocks, within the 4 units left: 4 |
| 12 | any | more units | 4 whole blocks |

A span of exactly 120 days counts 4 blocks under every kind; one of 121 days counts 5 under a per-period approval and 4 under the others.
